findings.issue: Task 3 delivers the `internal/view/view.go` Configure() wiring for all three progress views, but the test that asserts it — `TestViews_Configure` (verified at internal/view/view_test.go:99) — is owned by Task 4 in Wave 4. Task 3's Verify is `go test ./internal/query/... ./internal/view/...`, which passes green in Wave 3 while asserting nothing about the new PG 19 Configure cases. `TestView_VersionOK` (internal/view/view_test.go:224) is in the same file and the same situation. The acceptance criterion 'view.Configure() patches all three views' is therefore unprovable at the wave that implements it.
findings.fix: Move `internal/view/view_test.go` into Task 3's ownership and drop it from Task 4's Files to modify — the file cannot be co-owned by two tasks, and Task 3 is the task whose change it proves. Task 4 then adds no view-package edits. Alternatively keep it in Task 4 but move Task 4's view-test edits into Wave 3 as part of Task 3.

findings.issue: No task between the image publication and the Final Wave re-runs the Go test suite against the live PG 19 cluster. Task 8 (Wave 5) runs CI against *unmodified* `develop`, so it exercises the image but not the feature code. Task 9 (Wave 6) verifies only `./testing/e2e.sh`, which covers record→report, not the unit/integration suite. Task 4's `make test` runs in Wave 4, before the image exists, and the Per-task verification table explicitly permits 'or skip cleanly without the cluster'. Net effect: the PG 19 subtests added by Tasks 3 and 4 — the stated point of the feature — first actually execute in Task 10, three waves after they were written, where a failure means reopening Wave 3.
findings.fix: Add `make test` against the published image to Task 9's Verify (Task 9 already runs after the image is live), or move Task 8 to Wave 2 — it depends only on Task 1's image content, not on Wave 4 — so every downstream Go task verifies against a real PG 19 cluster. The second option also removes the inaccurate wave label noted below.

findings.issue: 8c: Task 1 description embeds decision rationale — 'This is the feature's first task and runs before any Go code, because its outcome decides whether the feature proceeds, absorbs a base-image migration, or pauses.' The `because` clause restates the three-step probe ladder that already lives in the Risks table and in the user-spec's «Ограничения».
findings.fix: Reduce to ordering language without the justification, e.g. 'Runs before any Go code — see the probe ladder in Risks.' Keep the rationale in the Risks table only.

findings.issue: 8c: Task 6 description embeds decision rationale — 'Also add the mixed-width diff guard from Decision 5b with its own case on the same harness, since this feature is what makes a mixed-width archive representable.' The `since` clause duplicates the reachability argument stated in full in Decision 5b.
findings.fix: Drop the `since` clause; the 'from Decision 5b' reference already carries the pointer: 'Also add the mixed-width diff guard from Decision 5b, with its own case on the same harness.'

findings.issue: Two decisions lack the required `Alternatives considered` field. Decision 8 ('Per-version query constants, never NULL-padded unified columns') and Decision 9 ('Autopilot assumption — branch and task granularity') both have Decision + Rationale only. All other decisions (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5a, 5b, 6, 7) carry all three fields.
findings.fix: Add `**Alternatives considered:**` to both. Decision 8: the NULL-padded unified column rejected by ADR [004] — already named in its rationale, so it only needs moving into the field. Decision 9: three separate per-screen tasks, rejected because all three share `internal/view/view.go` — likewise already stated in its rationale.

findings.issue: Task 10 (Pre-deploy QA) omits both `Files to modify` and `Files to read` entirely. Task 8, the other task with no code changes, handles this correctly — it writes `Files to modify: none` and still lists files to read. The inconsistency leaves it ambiguous whether the fields were considered or forgotten.
findings.fix: Add `- **Files to modify:** none` and a `- **Files to read:**` line pointing at the two documents the QA task is graded against: the user-spec («Как проверить» / «Критерии приёмки») and this tech-spec's Acceptance Criteria.

findings.issue: Task 6's `Files to modify` lists the directory `report/testdata/` (new goldens) rather than concrete paths — the same class of issue as the Task 4 glob fixed in round 1. The filenames are already determined: Testing Strategy names `report/testdata/report_record_progress_vacuum_pg{18,19}.golden`, and the repo confirms the convention (`report_record_bgwriter_pg14.golden`, `_pg17`, `_pg18` all exist).

Task 8's wave label reads 'Wave 5 (зависит от Wave 4 — действие пользователя)', but the task depends only on Task 1's image content (Wave 1). Nothing produced in Waves 2-4 feeds the image build. The stated dependency is stronger than the real one, and it is what creates the verification gap described above. This is not a wave-ordering violation — the placement is conservative, not incorrect — but the label is inaccurate.
findings.fix: Correct the label to name the real dependency (Wave 1), or move the task to Wave 2 and renumber the later waves.

findings.issue: 8c, low confidence: Task 2's description contains the decision marker `instead of` — 'return an error for a version it has no port mapping for, instead of falling back to the oldest cluster (Decision 5)'. Reading this as embedded rationale is arguable: the phrase describes what the change replaces (scope), not why, and it already cites Decision 5. Flagged for completeness, not as a clear violation.
findings.fix: No change needed if the intent is scope description. If tightening: 'Replace the test-connection helper's unmapped-version fallback with an error (Decision 5).'

findings.issue: The three new selector functions are never named — the spec writes them as `Select…Query(version) (string, int, [2]int)` with a literal ellipsis. `patterns.md:16` documents the project convention as `SelectStatXxxQuery(version int)`, and architecture.md lists the existing family (`SelectStatBgwriterQuery`, `SelectStatIOQuery`, `SelectStatWALQuery`, ...). Leaving the names to the implementer risks three inconsistent choices (`SelectProgressVacuumQuery` vs `SelectStatProgressVacuumQuery`).
findings.fix: Fix the three names in the Architecture section, following the underlying view names: `SelectStatProgressVacuumQuery`, `SelectStatProgressAnalyzeQuery`, `SelectStatProgressBasebackupQuery` (or whichever form is preferred — the point is to settle it in the spec).

summary: Round-2 re-validation: the round-1 critical is resolved and no new critical findings exist — status approved. Wave conflict detection is clean. Wave 4 holds four tasks (4, 5, 6, 7) with fully disjoint Files to modify sets; the deliberate hand-off of internal/stat/postgres_test.go from Task 4 to Task 6 is correctly recorded by the HTML comment and produces no overlap. Waves 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 hold a single task each, so no intra-wave collision is possible there. Wave dependency ordering is acyclic and every stated dependency runs strictly forward (Task 9 after Task 8 after Task 1; Tasks 5 and 6 after Task 3). All 45 file paths referenced across the tasks were verified to exist in the repository. Frontmatter is valid (created 2026-07-25, status draft, branch feature/pg19-compatibility-baseline, size M); every required section and subsection is present and substantive; the Risks table carries eleven realistic non-placeholder mitigations; no time-based estimates remain anywhere in the document (the round-1 'day-one' wording is gone); all skills resolve against the Execution Skills table and every named reviewer exists both in the catalog and as a file in ~/.claude/agents/. Five majors remain. Two are substantive: Task 3 ships the view.Configure wiring while the test asserting it lives in Task 4's file one wave later, and no task re-runs the Go suite against the published PG 19 image before Final QA — so the feature's PG 19 integration coverage is first exercised three waves after it is written. The other three are editorial: leftover rationale in the Task 1 and Task 6 descriptions, and missing 'Alternatives considered' on Decisions 8 and 9.
